subject: Performance SLOs + customer-led load test (FinWise)
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
To: Tom Brennan <tbrennan@finwise.com>
Cc: Sara Li <sara.li@finwise.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-25T14:05:00Z
Subject: Performance SLOs + customer-led load test (FinWise)

Hi Tom / Sara —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and next steps from our side so we all have the same picture: 

Key performance / SLO targets you listed
- 95th percentile latency goal: <= 450ms (inference end-to-end) for standard text-generation requests
- Streaming requirement: token-by-token streaming to client (server-sent events) with first-token < 200ms
- Concurrency: target sustained concurrency 60 concurrent sessions, peak bursts to 200 for up to 2 minutes
- Throughput: ~120 req/s sustained during peak business hours

Other constraints / asks
- Load tests to be run from FinWise (customer-led) against our staging endpoint (not prod)
- We will provide a time-limited staging API key and an IP allowlist for the test runner
- You’ll share the k6/Locust scripts you plan to run so we can validate they emulate real client behavior (streaming vs non-streaming)

Proposed next steps
1) Please confirm the test window you prefer (we suggested Tue 2027-04-27 02:00-05:00 UTC as low-impact for both sides).
2) Tom/Sara: share the k6/Locust scripts and the IP ranges you’ll use for the test.
3) Internal: Marissa / Rishi — can you provision a staging API key (scoped, limited tokens) and confirm the IP allowlist rules we need to add? Also validate we have a fallback plan (rate-limit/auto-throttle) if the test impacts other customers.

I’ll loop back once we have the scripts and your confirmation of the window.

Thanks —
Logan
Logan Wright
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
logan.wright@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0172
From: Tom Brennan <tbrennan@finwise.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Cc: Sara Li <sara.li@finwise.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-25T15:20:00Z
Subject: Re: Performance SLOs + customer-led load test (FinWise)

Logan — thanks for the clear recap. Agreed on the targets; a few clarifications from our side: 

- The 95th <= 450ms looks reasonable; we will also watch p50 and p99 as part of our validation.
- Streaming: critical that we can receive partial tokens for the first 1-2 seconds; we will simulate an interactive UI with backpressure.
- Concurrency: the 60 sustained / 200 peak is our target. We will run a 30-minute ramp to peak, hold for 10 minutes, then ramp down.

Test window: Tue 2027-04-27 02:00-05:00 UTC works for us.

Attached: a first-pass k6 script and a short Locustfile that mirror our frontend behavior (streaming emulation in the k6 script is done with chunked responses). We may tweak these tomorrow.

IP ranges: we will run from our cloud test runners (AWS us-west-2). Expected IPv4 ranges: 3.208.0.0/12, 44.192.0.0/10, plus ephemeral runners from 34.192.0.0/12. If you need concrete IPs, we can provide specific instances prior to the run.

Please provision the staging key and let us know the endpoint URL and any rate limits we should honor.

Thanks —
Tom
Tom Brennan
Head of Platform | FinWise
tbrennan@finwise.com
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-25T16:00:00Z
Subject: Fwd: Performance SLOs + customer-led load test (FinWise)

Marissa / Rishi — forwarding Tom’s reply and their initial k6/Locust files. Can you take the lead on: 
- Provisioning a time-limited staging API key (scope: inference endpoints only, token limit 100k tokens/day)
- Creating a staging endpoint URL to send to FinWise (should be on our sandbox cluster with no impact to prod)
- Confirming the IP allowlist approach: we can add the AWS ranges Tom gave as a stop-gap; if they provide instance IPs we’ll lock to those.
- Validate the scripts to ensure they exercise streaming properly (Marissa: would you confirm k6 chunk handling?)

Attachments referenced by Tom: k6-finwise-test.js, locustfile_finwise.py (attached to their email).

If you can turn around the staging key + endpoint + allowlist confirmation by EOD tomorrow (2027-04-26), we’ll lock the Tue window.

Thanks —
Logan
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Brennan <tbrennan@finwise.com>, Sara Li <sara.li@finwise.com>
Date: 2027-04-26T09:30:00Z
Subject: Re: Performance SLOs + customer-led load test (FinWise)

On Mon, Apr 25, 2027 at 16:00 Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com> wrote:
> Marissa / Rishi — forwarding Tom’s reply and their initial k6/Locust files. 

Thanks — I reviewed the scripts Tom attached. Quick notes and what we’ve provisioned: 

What we did
- Provisioned a staging API key: FINWISE-STG-20270427 (scoped to sandbox; expires 2027-04-29 00:00:00 UTC). I’ll DM the key to Tom (security).
- Staging endpoint: https://staging-api.redwood.com/finwise/v1/generate (TLS, sandbox cluster in us-west-2)
- Added temporary allowlist entries for the AWS ranges Tom provided (3.208.0.0/12, 44.192.0.0/10, 34.192.0.0/12). These are in place and will be tightened to instance IPs if and when they share them.
- Rate-limits: no global account throttles on staging, but we enabled a tenant-level safeguard that will auto-throttle at 350 req/s for 2 minutes if upstream latency rises > 1s.

Script validation notes
- k6 script (k6-finwise-test.js): it does a good job at simulating chunked streaming via repeated chunk endpoints. We’ll run a dry run on our side to validate the streaming client behavior and token accounting.
- Locust (locustfile_finwise.py): good for session-level concurrency emulation; note that it doesn’t currently simulate partial-token consumption - that’s fine for throughput tests but won’t exercise streaming paths.

Attachments (uploaded): k6-finwise-test.js (validated), locustfile_finwise.py (validated).

Request for FinWise
- Please provide final instance IPs (or confirm the ranges) by 2027-04-26 16:00 UTC so we can lock the allowlist.
- Confirm you’ve received the staging key via secure channel.

We’ll run an internal dry run Mon 2027-04-26 20:00 UTC to confirm no noisy neighbors and to baseline the staging cluster. If that looks good we’ll be ready for Tue windows.


Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
From: Tom Brennan <tbrennan@finwise.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Cc: Sara Li <sara.li@finwise.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-26T10:10:00Z
Subject: Re: Performance SLOs + customer-led load test (FinWise)

Marissa — got the key via our secure channel, thanks. We’ll lock the test runner instances and provide the specific public IPs by 16:00 UTC today. Confirming the Tue 2027-04-27 02:00-05:00 UTC window.

We’ll also send a short post-test report (p50/p95/p99, token counts, error rates) within 2 hours of test completion. If anything unexpected shows up on your end during the dry run, ping me on Slack and we’ll pause.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Tom
